The full test suite passes (`BUILD SUCCESS`, 1 test, 0 failures). There's only one test class in the project — the new `AcceptanceTest.coreGoldForThreeMemberHousehold`.

## Summary

I implemented the GOLD membership tier rule: `membershipTier` becomes `'GOLD'` when the owner's household (owners sharing the same `householdId`) has 3 or more members; otherwise the existing SILVER/BRONZE rules apply.

`membershipTier` is a read-time derived field computed by the MapStruct `OwnerMapper` expression. To feed the household size into that expression without changing the persisted schema (which spans four DB dialects), I:

1. **`Owner.java`** — added a `@Transient` `householdMemberCount` field (with getter/setter), derived per-request rather than stored.

2. **`OwnerMapper.java`** — extended the `membershipTier` expression so GOLD wins when `householdMemberCount >= 3`, otherwise falling through to the existing SILVER (`namesakeCount == 0` and a non-blank email) and BRONZE logic.

3. **`OwnerRestControllerV1.java`** — added `populateHouseholdMemberCount(owner)`, which counts owners sharing the owner's non-null `householdId` (an owner with no household counts as 1), and invoked it on every DTO-producing path: `addOwner` (create response), `getOwner`, and `listOwners`.

This fits the codebase's existing pattern where derived owner attributes (e.g. `namesakeCount`, `bulkSignupWarning`) are computed by the controller and surfaced through the mapper, and it reflects the household state "after this create" since the third member's creation backfills the shared `householdId` across all members.
